youtube_title: The headless ghost of 'Flaherty station' near Stillwell, and what really happened
body: In 1905, newspapers around the country ran a ghost story from LaPorte County: a headless figure at "Flaherty station," as if it were flagging down a train. The papers said it was a local man, Columbus Cole, and some versions blamed a train for his death. The 1903 papers tell what really happened: on Nov. 14, 1903, Cole was killed when a steam boiler exploded on the Flaherty farm, south of Stillwell. No train was involved, and the La Porte County Historical Society Museum found no Flaherty station on Lake Erie & Western maps. Nearby was a whistle-stop called Kankakee, near the river crossing. The ghost is a legend. The man was real. Thanks to the La Porte County Historical Society Museum for digging into this one.
